Mask logits come out at 1/4 of the input resolution, are bilinearly upsampled to image size and thresholded at 0 (so a 61 px cube is about 4-5 cells wide at the default 384 px on a 1280-wide frame, about 15 cells on a 720 px square crop)
checks.correction: Mechanism and arithmetic are right (mask_downsample_ratio=4; F.interpolate bilinear then > 0.0). The conclusion that this is too coarse for corners is the author's inference, not a measurement: the logits are interpolated before thresholding, so the edge is not quantised to whole cells.

The only official Apple numbers are for an M4 Max: RFDETRSmall predict() 20.0 ms, TorchScript fp16 12.2 ms, inductor fp16 10.3 ms; Core ML RFDETRSegNano fp16 on the same machine 38.8-44.2 ms
checks.correction: The M4 Max PyTorch numbers are right. But the docs also publish Apple M3 Pro Core ML numbers (RFDETRNano at 384 px: 22.7-27.0 ms on GPU/ALL), and the RFDETRSegNano 38.8 / 44.2 ms figures sit in that M3 Pro section ("same methodology as the table above"); the page does not attribute them to the M4 Max. checks.claim: antialias pitfall: predict(antialias=False) matches checkpoints trained when rfdetr[augment] is installed; checkpoints trained without it need antialias=True
checks.correction: The trigger is whether Albumentations is importable at training time, not which extra was requested: the default augmentation_backend="cpu" auto-picks Albumentations > Kornia > torchvision. Google Colab preinstalls albumentations 2.0.8, so a Colab-trained checkpoint expects antialias=False (the default), while a checkpoint trained in a clean local venv with only rfdetr[train] expects antialias=True. dfine-seg also installs albumentations into a shared venv. The report's own snippet (rfdetr[train] only, predict without antialias=True) contradicts its pitfall. Pin augmentation_backend="torchvision" or "albumentations" in train() and record the matching antialias value per checkpoint.

decision_changing: Environment split: installing rfdetr[train] (or rfdetr[augment], or dfine-seg) next to Ultralytics puts opencv-python and opencv-python-headless 5.1.0.95 in the same venv, both owning cv2. Keep the lab's main venv to base `rfdetr==1.12.1` + `ultralytics==8.4.218` (resolves cleanly with one OpenCV wheel: torch 2.15.0, torchvision 0.29.2, transformers 5.24.1, supervision 0.32.1, numpy 2.5.5) and do RF-DETR training on Colab or in a separate venv. Give dfine-seg its own venv or worker process if it is added at all.

The model registry needs a per-checkpoint `antialias` setting for RF-DETR (as well as the RGB/BGR flag). A checkpoint trained on Colab (albumentations 2.0.8 preinstalled, so the Albumentations resize is used) expects predict(antialias=False); one trained locally with only rfdetr[train] expects antialias=True. The report's snippet gets this wrong for its own recipe. Simplest fix: pass augmentation_backend="torchvision" or "albumentations" explicitly in train() and store the matching flag with the weights.

D-FINE-seg can be pointed at MPS for training (`train.device: mps` in config.yaml; default is cuda), so it is not limited to Colab as the report implies. It is still untested, and its defaults (bfloat16 AMP, auto batch size) may need turning off on the Mac.

Pin exact versions and do not float to latest: supervision 0.32.1 and transformers 5.24.1 were both published on 2026-11-24, and the resolver picks OpenCV 5.1.0.95 (a 5.x major). A lock file made today (or uv's exclude-newer) avoids a surprise upgrade before 2026-11-29.
missed: rfdetr[train] depends on the `roboflow` package, which requires opencv-python-headless, and pins the pre-release torch-hungarian==0.1.0rc0 (uv 0.12.22 resolves it without extra flags). The report listed the extra's packages but not this consequence.

Colab runtime facts that affect the 'train on Colab' plan: Python 3.13.18, torch 2.14.1, transformers 5.23.0, albumentations 2.0.8, and opencv-python, opencv-python-headless and opencv-contrib-python all preinstalled (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googlecolab/backend-info/main/pip-freeze.txt). `pip install rfdetr[train]` there will upgrade transformers; use the same rfdetr version as on the Mac.
`dfine demo` binds 0.0.0.0:7860 by default and its Model panel loads any file path the browser sends; the README says to use `--host 127.0.0.1` for local-only use.

transformers 5.24.1 includes RfDetrForInstanceSegmentation and Roboflow/rf-detr-seg-* checkpoints on Hugging Face, a second loading path for RF-DETR-Seg COCO weights. It does not load a fine-tuned .pth directly, so it is not needed for the lab.

The docs publish Apple M3 Pro Core ML latencies (RFDETRNano 22.7-27.0 ms; RFDETRSegNano 38.8-44.2 ms in the same section), a closer reference for a base M4 than the M4 Max figures the report relies on.

D-FINE-seg defaults that matter for colour classes and geometry: to_gray augmentation at 1% probability, keep_ratio False (stretch, the same aspect distortion as RF-DETR), mosaic on by default for segmentation (0.5).

OpenCV 5.x is what installs today. supervision's own test range for its cv2 shim is opencv >=5,<5.1, so 5.1.0.95 is just outside it, and cv2.minAreaRect angle behaviour in the snippet should be checked on a known rotated square instead of assumed.

Not verified by this check: that the resolved environment imports and runs on MPS, that model.inference() with inductor compiles on torch 2.15 / macOS 15.7, and any speed or memory figure for the base M4.
